name: Oberperfuss
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny municipality at the foot of the Rangger Köpfl at the entrance to the Sellrain Valley, near Innsbruck, birthplace of the cartographer Peter Anich.
beschreibung:
Oberperfuss lies at an altitude of 812 metres at the entrance to the Sellrain Valley, at the foot of the Rangger Köpfl and only around 20 kilometres from Innsbruck. The municipality in the district of Innsbruck-Land has over 3,000 inhabitants and is today a commuter community in which rural tradition and around 40 businesses shape the village scene.

Oberperfuss is known as the birthplace of the cartographer Peter Anich (1723–1766), who created the famous „Anich map“ of Tyrol on behalf of Maria Theresa. In the village centre stands the baroque Parish Church of Saint Margaret, completed in 1733 according to plans by Gallus Gratl.

The Oberperfuss mountain railways provide access to the local mountain Rangger Köpfl in winter and summer, while the Anich-Hueber Museum commemorates the famous sons of the village.
text:
Overview

Oberperfuss is located in the sun-drenched Western Low Mountain Terrace in the Tyrolean district of Innsbruck-Land, about 15 kilometres west of Innsbruck on an elevated plateau above the Inn Valley at an altitude of 812 metres. This charming residential municipality has around 3,120 residents and covers an area of 15.3 square kilometres, reaching from agricultural terraces above the river up through dense mountain forests to the prominent peak of Mount Rosskogel (2,646 m) in the Stubai Alps. Oberperfuss captivates visitors with its unspoilt village ambiance, picturesque scattered hamlets such as Berg, Völsgasse, and Aigling, and expansive panoramic vistas across the Inn Valley towards the jagged limestone cliffs of the Nordkette range. Connected directly to the year-round outdoor paradise of the Rangger Köpfl mountain, the village seamlessly blends tranquil rural charm with exceptional leisure activities in all seasons.

History

Human settlement on the sunny plateau dates back to the late Bronze Age and Roman antiquity. The village was first documented in 1083 under the name Perlves, derived from a pre-Roman local field name. Oberperfuss gained international fame in the 18th century as the cradle of modern alpine cartography: it was the birthplace of self-taught farmer and cartographer Peter Anich (1723–1766). Commissioned by Empress Maria Theresa, Anich and his colleague Blasius Hueber surveyed and drew the groundbreaking Atlas Tyrolensis, the first accurate topographic map of Tyrol. The Baroque Parish Church of St. Margaret, designed by architect Gallus Gratl, preserves a remarkable sundial constructed by Peter Anich on the cemetery wall, next to his honoured grave. In the village centre, the dedicated Peter Anich Museum celebrates his extraordinary life, exhibiting original celestial globes and historic surveying tools.

Getting There

Oberperfuss is quickly and easily reached from Innsbruck by private vehicle or public transport. By car, take the Inntal Autobahn A12, exit at Zirl-Ost or Kematen, and follow the provincial road L11 through Kematen, connecting to the L233 which ascends directly to Oberperfuss in just 20 minutes from Innsbruck city centre. Rail passengers arrive at Innsbruck Central Station or the nearby regional station of Unterperfuss on the Arlberg Railway line. From Innsbruck Central Station and the central bus terminal, modern VVT regional bus routes 461 and 462 operate at frequent half-hourly intervals, providing direct links without transfers straight to the village centre and the valley terminal of the Peter-Anich-Bahn cable car.

Tips

The outdoor hub of the municipality is the Rangger Köpfl mountain, accessed easily by the modern Peter-Anich-Bahn gondola. In winter, this sunny family ski area offers 17 kilometres of immaculate ski slopes and a spectacular natural toboggan run: extending over eight kilometres from the Sulzstich mountain station down via Stiglreith to the valley floor, it ranks among the longest and most scenic sledging tracks in Tyrol, illuminated for night tobogganing on selected evenings. In summer, the scenic Rangger Köpfl reservoir lake, child-friendly theme trails, and alpine summit ascents to the Rosskogel (2,646 m) provide unforgettable days in nature. Cultural explorers must not miss the Peter Anich Museum, and a stroll along the local panoramic paths offers glorious views over the Stubai and Inn valleys.
